harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Established an AIDE-based file-integrity baseline for /etc on node1: installed AIDE, added an explicit '/etc NORMAL' rule for full content+hash coverage (default config only applied metadata-only PERMS to the broad /etc catch-all), initialized and activated the database (/var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz, 39284 entries), verified detection works by modifying and reverting /etc/hosts (AIDE flagged SHA512/SHA3-256 diffs), added a daily cron job (/etc/cron.d/aide-check) so future changes are checked and logged automatically, then rebuilt the baseline to capture that final state cleanly. Completed the mandatory single-node restart-evidence protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id and a clean AIDE check, issued a backgrounded systemctl reboot whose acknowledgement returned before disconnect, polled until node1 was reachable again, confirmed the boot_id changed (21de1f79-e793-4c36-923a-f4af0bbea55e -> 0dfad7e1-05d9-4f68-a6bd-89115a4876bf) proving a real restart occurred, and verified post-restart that the baseline database hash on disk was unchanged, crond was active, and a fresh AIDE check still reported zero differences.
actions_performed: Installed the aide package on node1 via dnf
Appended '/etc NORMAL' to /etc/aide.conf so all of /etc gets content-hash coverage, not just the default metadata-only PERMS catch-all
Ran aide --init and promoted aide.db.new.gz to aide.db.gz as the active baseline
Ran aide --check to confirm a clean initial baseline (no differences)
Modified /etc/hosts as a reversible test, confirmed AIDE detected and reported the change (exit code 4, hash diff shown), then restored the file and reconfirmed clean state
Added /etc/cron.d/aide-check to run 'aide --check' daily and log to /var/log/aide/aide-cron.log for ongoing change reporting
Ran aide --update to fold the new cron file into the baseline and reconfirmed a clean check afterward
Captured pre-restart boot_id and baseline/cron health as the healthy baseline
Issued a backgrounded 'systemctl reboot' on node1 so acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again, confirming the reboot occurred via connection errors followed by successful reconnection
Verified changed boot_id post-restart and re-checked AIDE database hash, crond status, and aide --check result to confirm full recovery

evidence.requirement: AIDE installed and configured with /etc content-hash coverage
evidence.summary: Confirmed CentOS Stream 10, aide not initially installed; installed aide; inspected default aide.conf showing only metadata-level PERMS for the broad /etc rule; appended an explicit '/etc NORMAL' rule for full content hashing.

evidence.requirement: Integrity baseline database initialized and activated
evidence.summary: Ran aide --init (completed with multiple hash algorithms computed), promoted aide.db.new.gz to aide.db.gz, and confirmed aide --check reports 'NO differences' against the new baseline (39283 entries).

evidence.requirement: Baseline actually detects later changes to /etc files
evidence.summary: Appended a marker line to /etc/hosts; aide --check exited 4 and reported the exact SHA512/SHA3-256 change for /etc/hosts. Restored the file and reconfirmed aide --check returns clean (exit 0).

evidence.requirement: Ongoing automated reporting mechanism for future /etc changes
evidence.summary: Added /etc/cron.d/aide-check (daily aide --check logged to /var/log/aide/aide-cron.log) via active crond; confirmed AIDE correctly flagged the new cron file as an added entry, then updated/re-activated the baseline (aide --update, copied to aide.db.gz) to reflect the final /etc state, with a subsequent clean check (39284 entries, no differences).
Captured pre-restart boot_id (21de1f79-e793-4c36-923a-f4af0bbea55e), aide.db.gz hash/size, cron file contents, and active crond status as the healthy baseline.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'sleep 2 && systemctl reboot' returned 'reboot scheduled, ack returned' immediately, before the node disconnected.

evidence.requirement: node1 changed boot identity proving a real restart
evidence.summary: Subsequent polls returned connection reset/timeout errors during the reboot window, then a successful exec returned a new boot_id (0dfad7e1-05d9-4f68-a6bd-89115a4876bf) and fresh uptime -s timestamp, differing from the pre-restart boot_id.

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of integrity baseline and cron reporting
evidence.summary: After restart, aide.db.gz hash on disk matched the pre-restart hash exactly, crond was active, the cron file was intact, and a fresh aide --check reported zero differences (39284 entries), confirming full recovery of the integrity baseline and its automated reporting mechanism.
